definition: Organising someone's calendar and appointments.
business_context_example: Diary management for three directors is a full-time job on its own.

definition: Having two appointments at the same time by mistake.
business_context_example: The meeting room is double-booked at eleven, so one of them moves.

definition: To move something to a different time or date.
business_context_example: Can we reschedule Thursday's call to Friday morning?

definition: An available period of time in a schedule.
business_context_example: There's a free slot at 3:15 if twenty minutes is enough.

definition: To reserve time in a calendar so nobody books it.
business_context_example: I block out Friday afternoons for admin, and I defend it.

definition: An automatic reply saying you are away.
business_context_example: Set your out of office before you leave, not from the airport.

definition: To do someone's work while they are away.
business_context_example: Radost is covering for me next week, so copy her in.

definition: To communicate and work together with another person or team.
business_context_example: Please liaise with the venue about parking for the guests.

definition: To organise different people or parts so they work together.
business_context_example: She coordinates six trainers across four cities every week.

definition: To contact someone again because they haven't replied or acted.
business_context_example: I'll chase up the signed forms this afternoon.

definition: To send a document to a group of people.
business_context_example: Circulate the agenda 24 hours before the meeting, please.

definition: A short official note sent inside an organisation.
business_context_example: A one-paragraph memo replaced what used to be a meeting.

definition: A file sent together with an email.
business_context_example: The attachment was 40 megabytes, so it bounced back.

definition: To confirm that you have received something.
business_context_example: Please acknowledge receipt so I know it arrived.

definition: Mail sent with proof of sending and delivery.
business_context_example: The contract went by registered post, not email.

definition: A company or person delivering packages quickly.
business_context_example: The courier collects at 4 pm, so it needs to be sealed by 3:45.

definition: The organised way documents are stored and found.
business_context_example: A filing system only works if two people can use it.

definition: To store old records that are no longer used daily.
business_context_example: We archive files after three years and keep them for ten.

definition: Keeping accurate written information about activities.
business_context_example: Good record keeping is boring until an inspection arrives.

definition: Typing information into a computer system.
business_context_example: Two hours of data entry every Monday, and errors dropped when we split it.

definition: A document of rows and columns used for calculations.
business_context_example: The whole schedule lives in one spreadsheet, which worries me.

definition: A ready-made format used as a starting point.
business_context_example: Use the template so every certificate looks the same.

definition: To destroy paper documents by cutting them into strips.
business_context_example: Anything with a client name on it gets shredded, not binned.

definition: Documents that must be destroyed securely.
business_context_example: The confidential waste bin is emptied every second Tuesday.

definition: Everyday items a workplace needs, like paper and pens.
business_context_example: Office supplies are ordered on the first Monday of the month.

definition: An official document ordering goods or services.
business_context_example: No purchase order, no delivery. The supplier is strict about it.

definition: Counting everything the company has in store.
business_context_example: The stock take showed we had 400 unused workbooks.

definition: To be nearly out of something.
business_context_example: We're running low on printer paper again.

definition: The buildings, rooms and equipment an organisation uses.
business_context_example: Facilities handles the heating, not the IT department.

definition: A formal ask for something to be repaired.
business_context_example: I raised a maintenance request for the broken blind on Tuesday.

definition: The area where visitors arrive and are greeted.
business_context_example: Meet me at reception at ten to nine.

definition: An identity card given to guests inside a building.
business_context_example: Every visitor badge is returned at the end of the day.

definition: To record your arrival in a book or system.
business_context_example: Contractors sign in at the gate, staff use the card reader.

definition: The introduction and basic training given to new arrivals.
business_context_example: Safety induction takes 20 minutes and everyone does it.

definition: To arrange flights, trains and hotels.
business_context_example: I book travel on Wednesdays so the prices are comparable.

definition: A document listing money spent on work that should be paid back.
business_context_example: Submit the expense report with receipts by the 5th.

definition: A fixed daily amount given to cover travel costs.
business_context_example: The per diem is 45 euro a day, no receipts needed.

definition: Payment for using your own car for work travel.
business_context_example: Mileage is claimed at 0.30 euro per kilometre.

definition: To decide what matters most and do it first.
business_context_example: When everything is urgent, somebody has to prioritise out loud.

definition: A written list of tasks that need doing.
business_context_example: A to-do list with 30 items is a wish, not a plan.

definition: The parts of a business that support operations without meeting clients.
business_context_example: The back office processes 200 enrolments a month, quietly.

definition: The sequence of steps a task goes through.
business_context_example: We mapped the enrolment workflow and removed three steps.

definition: To approve a document formally.
business_context_example: The manager signs off every invoice above 500 euro.

definition: A printed version of a document.
business_context_example: Bring a hard copy to the meeting, the projector is unreliable.

definition: To write the official record of a meeting.
business_context_example: Can you minute the meeting? I'll be presenting.

definition: A saved group of email addresses used together.
business_context_example: Update the distribution list, two people on it have left.

definition: Small routine office tasks that take time but little thought.
business_context_example: Petty admin eats a morning if you let it arrive in pieces.

definition: Stored in the records for future reference.
business_context_example: We already have her contract on file from last year.

definition: To complete and return something within a period.
business_context_example: We turn around certificates within two working days.
translation_bg: да обработя и върна в срок

definition: To stay in control of work so it doesn't build up.
business_context_example: Twenty minutes daily keeps me on top of the inbox.
